newsitem.title: UK: Highest IATA passenger growth seen for 1997-98.
newsitem.headline: Highest IATA passenger growth seen for 1997-98.

text.p: International Air Transport Association (IATA) forecasts show combined domestic and international passenger traffic is set to average 6.3 percent for 1996-2000 period, IATA economist, Francois Dormoy said.
The two years 1997-98 will experience the highest annual average growth levels of 6.8 percent, he told IATA's 10th annual Air Transport Outlook conference on Wednesday.
This will see total scheduled traffic flow rise to 1.725 billion passengers by the year 2000 from 1.36 billion passengers this year.
"What we have now are annual growth areas of seven percent in international passengers and six percent in domestic passengers, giving an overall rates of more than six percent," said Dormoy.

Other highlights from the IATA forecast include Asia-Pacific (excluding Hawaii) representing 38.2 percent of the total world international scheduled traffic by the year 2000, compared to the present 34.5 percent, he added.

Europe will remain the most important world region for the number of international scheduled passengers which will increase from 224 million in 1995 to over 308 million by 2000 and nearer 450 million "if we add charter traffic" said Dormoy.
North American will remain the second largest international market but by 2000 its lead over Asia will be down from 34 million passengers in 1995 to about 20 million.

Average distances travelled will increase from 3,600 kilometres to 3,660 kilometres for 1995-2000 which, although only 50 kilometres, is significant when averaged over 500 million passengers," Darmoy said. -- Air Cargo Newsroom tel+44 171 542 7706 Fax+44 171 542 5017.
